text:
michelle: Quick heads-up, perf dashboard shows a ~18% p95 increase on host-side request parsing around 09:12 UTC. correlates with spike in writev syscalls. attaching quick notes.
raj: I saw that too, looks like smallwrite batching dropped, maybe due to new kernel-selection rollout?
oliver: Which rollout? kernel-selection 2.1 went live 09:00, but that affects GPU kernels — shouldn't touch ingress path.
michelle: True, but we rolled a batching heuristic tweak in proxy at 08:50 that flips min_batch_size -> 1 for latency-sensitive routes. suspecting fragmentation + writev penalty.
jordan: TL;DR: tiny frames -> lots of writev ops -> HPACK/emulation overhead on gRPC -> CPU swing.
marta: Can we reproduce locally? I can try a 1000 req/s short prompt workload and capture strace.
raj: pls also capture sendmsg/writev counts, and kernel selector flags from /proc/sys/some_flag? :) infra-bot: Deployment 2026-03-17T08:47Z: proxy/batching-heuristic v3 promoted to canary (10%).
michelle: Good call — infra-bot shows canary. I'll bisect canary vs stable.
oliver: Attached microprofile sample from canary: p95 parse+serialize = 12.3ms (stable: 9.8ms). flame: top stacks show writev, hpack::compress, Tokenizer::normalize
marta: sample run command I used:
```
wrk -t8 -c200 -d60 --latency http://proxy.local/generate -s ./short_prompt.lua
strace -f -e trace=writev -c -o writev.out ./client
```
raj: Interesting: tokenization CPU also up ~2% — could be UTF8 normalization path hit more due to splitting change.
jordan: Could caching be getting less effective? KV hit rate dropped from 98%->93% around spike.
michelle: yes KV cache telemetry shows increased eviction churn on host preproc shard 7 at 09:10 — correlate with canary pods scaling.
oliver: Theory: canary changed minibatch hint -> more micro-batches, lowering batching efficiency and increasing unique prefixes hitting KV.
marta: If so, quick mitigation: revert minibatch hint or increase prefix cache size for host shard 7 until we have a root cause.
raj: Also evaluate combining small writes into single writev (coalesce) in proxy before HPACK encode. cheap win.
jordan: Patch idea (proto): coalesce consecutive small frames <256B for same stream into 1 writev; respect latency SLO with timer 150us.
michelle: Agree. Let's try a canary with coalesce timer first. Olvier/Jordan to prototype. Marta to run perf harness and capture writev counts + KV hit rate. I'll coordinate rollback if canary >5% p95 regression.
oliver: I'll open a quick PR with flags: proxy.coalesce_small_frames.enabled=true, .max_aggregate_size=1024, .latency_timer_us=150
marta: test matrix: (stable, canary, canary+coalesce) x (100, 1000 req/s) capture p50/p95, writev ops/s, kvcache_hit%
infra-bot: Canary promotion blocked: observed p95 degradation 18% > threshold (10%).
michelle: Rolling canary back to 0% now. Thanks all — follow-up: collect traces and kernel-selector configs for machines that served shard 7.
raj: I'll push a small sampling agent to collect /proc and kernel cmdline + proxy flags for the affected nodes.
jordan: Note for postmortem: avoid changing minibatch heuristics and kernel-selector flags in same deploy window; they interact badly.
marta: I'll upload the strace + perf samples to the triage folder and link in thread after upload.
michelle: perfect — moving to incident channel if we see this reoccur. :thumbsup:
